title: What a Black Hole Really Is and How One Forms
post_title: What a Black Hole Really Is and How One Forms | QuantaTale
post_description: What black holes are, how massive stars collapse into them and how scientists find them, from NASA and ESA. Sources: National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://science.nasa.gov/universe/black-holes/ and European Space Agency https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/science/black-holes #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: What kind of object is so dense that even light cannot escape it? Black holes are not really holes but huge amounts of matter packed into tiny spaces. Their gravity is so intense that not even light can get out from beyond a boundary called the event horizon. One kind is born when a massive star runs out of fuel and explodes in a supernova. As the core collapses, the outer layers rebound and are thrown into space. If the core left behind is more than three times the Sun's mass, it keeps being crushed into a smaller and smaller volume. Black holes neither emit nor reflect light, so scientists detect them by how they affect their surroundings. Even the closest known black hole, Gaia BH1, is incredibly far away. Our galaxy's central black hole, Sagittarius A*, is 4 million times the Sun's mass. In 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope produced the earliest direct picture of one, a dark silhouette against glowing matter.
